page.layout: One page of running text. Running head and page number at the top. Heading "INTENTIO I." with its subtitle, then "ARTICVLVS I." and the body in one column. Catchword at the lower right. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: paratas avolare. Hæc sunt quæ Deo dante extra dubium ponenda suscepimus; non quidem seorsum singula probando; sed ex iis quæ natura suggeret, vel singulis, vel simul junctis, per necessariam consequentiam omnia deducendo. Age igitur Lector, & hanc partem non ingratam nec inutilem gratus accipe.
main_text.head: INTENTIO I.
De diversitate partium compositarum, ex quarum harmonia totum resultat.
ARTICVLVS I.
main_text.p: Superius necessario non pauca præmisimus, quæ id quod propositum fuimus ostendere non obscure designant; Non tantum prima elementa in misto seu mavis composito manere, sed diversissimas quibus mistum constat, particulas, ex iis primis rerum principiis diversimode constructas; quas secundas, docendi gratia vocare liceat. Ex his secundis varie coëuntibus, tertiæ fiunt non minus quàm secundæ inter se differentes. Eundem in modum, & ex tertiis quartæ, & ex quartis quintæ fieri intelliguntur. Ad cuius rei confessionem nos vel invitos ducit experientia in rei cuiusvis dissolutione. Quippe, res in ea resolvitur, ex quibus componitur. Atqui compositum naturale non primo resolvitur in prima illa elementa, sed in partes quasdam inter se natura discrepantes; quarum singulæ species rursus in alios multiplices dividuntur; & hæ in alias minutiores concluduntur. Sæpiusque hæc partium diversarum in minutiores semper diversas subdivisio repetitur. Exemplo sit uva, quæ pressa in mustum

page.notes: The first word of the body is a large initial S joined to "Vperius", read as "Superius". "Vperius" is a vowel, so I wrote U-based spelling per rule 5 only where it fits; the V/U in the initial is set by the woodcut letter and not checked further. Long s is printed as f in many words (fuscepimus, feorsum, fingula, miftum, constructas, diffolutione, refolvitur); all are written with plain s. The catchword "muftum" is read as "mustum". A small red mark at the foot of the page is a stain or stamp and is not transcribed.
